requirements.requirement: Repair bin/import.py to parse the documented 5/12/4-character fixed-width layout and emit CSV columns id, name, and quantity while preserving leading-zero IDs and trimming only right-hand name padding.
requirements.summary: The installed importer slices fields at the documented boundaries, preserves IDs as strings, uses right-only space trimming for names, and writes CSV safely. Fixture and edge-case assertions directly verify leading zeros, retained leading name spaces, removed right padding, and correct quoting of comma-containing names.

requirements.requirement: Reject wrong-length records and records with nonnumeric quantities into rejects.txt with their line numbers.
requirements.summary: Direct fixture and isolated edge-case tests show both invalid quantity and wrong-length records excluded from CSV and recorded in rejects.txt with correct source line numbers.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the original staged input in /srv/legacy2/fixed-width-import-recovery.
requirements.summary: The input remained in place with its original 72-byte size, timestamp during installation, and baseline SHA-256 hash before modification, after installation, after conversion, and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: RHEL 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64 are unchanged across the lifecycle snapshots and restart. The importer executes and passes tests using the installed Python 2.7.5 runtime.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for managed node node1.
requirements.summary: The protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart importer, data, and artifacts were observed; restart scheduling was acknowledged; two temporary SSH failures bounded the disruption; the boot ID changed; and SSH, platform, files, importer execution, CSV, and rejects recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The importer correctly handles the documented fixed-width format, preserves IDs and the original input, trims names correctly, rejects malformed records with line numbers, remains compatible with the unchanged RHEL 7 platform, and recovers fully after the mandatory node restart. Only minor temporary-file hygiene issues remain.
limitations: Package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so package health could not be independently compared; no package-changing executor command is shown.
The fixed lifecycle collector does not inventory the task directory, so file-level conclusions rely on the detailed executor commands and the authored preparation baseline.
Four low-risk temporary artifacts remained after execution, although none affects demonstrated task functionality.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: No causally unrelated or reverted troubleshooting mutation was identified. The failed initial installation attempt created the source later installed by the corrective command, while its backup and compilation were reasonable safeguards or validation. Required output generation, edge testing, and restart verification were bounded and directly related to the outcomes. Hygiene is reduced for retained low-risk temporary residue: /tmp/import.py.before and /tmp/import.py.newc from cmd-f16daf60ecb94f52, the restart log from cmd-bdb8ce01907f47bd, and /tmp/output.post-restart.csv from cmd-d59ca5f7c36d4a5f. These remained in the final snapshot. The edge-test directory created by cmd-ff2bd052067b46a4 was removed by its trap. No failed services, new socket exposure, OS/kernel change, or other damaging residue is shown.
